articles.text:
F. WORD ORDER

In Unit 2 we observed that the second part of verb phrases—the infinitive form of the verb—occurs at the end of the sentence: Ich kann es Ihnen hier auf dem Stadtplan zeigen (I can show it to you here on the map of the city). The other part of verb phrases, the verb form that has the personal ending, is seen to occur at or near the beginning of the sentence. This form is called the finite verb form.

The lesson provides several examples to illustrate the position of the finite verb form: Sie kommt heute nicht (She's not coming today); Das Museum ist am Markt (The museum is on the market place); Das weiss ich leider nicht (I am sorry I don't know that); Dort ist der Portier (There's the doorman); In zehn Minuten sind Sie da (You'll be there in ten minutes); Wo ist die Strassenbahn-haltestelle? (Where is the streetcar stop?). In these examples the finite verb form is always the second element of the sentence. It can be preceded by a pronoun, a noun and its specifier, a specifier or pointing word, an adverb indicating time, location or manner, a prepositional phrase and its object, or a question word.

In questions without question words and in commands, the finite verb form is the first element: Fährt denn kein Omnibus dahin? (Isn't there a bus that goes there?) and Gehen Sie hier durch den Park (Go through the park here).

The lesson emphasizes that students should observe this positioning of the finite verb and remember that in yes–no questions and imperative sentences, the finite verb moves to the first position.
